description:
Build any crypto agent: describe the goal in plain words and get the stack to build it from — framework, wallet, trading and swap venues, x402 payments, onchain data, on Base, Solana or any listed chain. USE WHEN someone wants to build an onchain or crypto agent and says what it should do — "a trading agent on Base", "an ElizaOS agent that charges via x402", "a TypeScript agent with a policy-controlled wallet". This is the first call for a build goal: goal → stack here, then onchain_agent_get_deploy_spec once per pick → install steps. It returns a trust-ranked stack of real directory resources — bucketed into slots (framework, wallet, payments, trading, data, MCP tooling, security; live agents someone else runs are kept out of trading), each pick carrying its Sato Score, liveness, deploy-spec status, github_url and a `preflight_summary` (the Preflight verdict from Sato Hub's records, its rule and the readings it turned on), plus honest gaps where the directory has no strong match. A standard the goal names (x402, ERC-8004, A2A, MCP) and a runtime it names (TypeScript/Node, Python) lift the picks that implement or run on it, and a wallet control it names (a policy, spending limit, session keys, permissions) lifts wallets whose own tags or one-liner name one — quoted in the reason, self-reported. `save_stack_url` opens the goal in the Sato Hub planner for the person you are building for. When the goal is on Base with a wallet, swap, trading or x402 payments and names TypeScript/Node or no runtime, `starter` points at a TypeScript GitHub template repo built by Sato Hub (holds no key, signs nothing, not audited; `runtime_basis` says whether the goal named the runtime) — never a pick. A goal naming another runtime gets none. Before anything is installed, connected, paid or traded, onchain_agent_preflight with a pick's full_check args returns every evidence line. Ranking reflects openness/activity/verifiability — never a safety, quality, or returns judgment; a Preflight `unknown` means no record, not a problem. Read-only.

Example: { goal: "trading agent on Base with x402 payments", chain: "Base" }

goal.description: What the agent should do, in plain words — e.g. 'trading agent on Base with x402 payments'

verified_only.description: True = only picks whose documented install was reproduced in a container by Sato Hub. Slots with no verified pick are reported in `gaps` rather than widened.

name: onchain_agent_recommend_stack
title: Build any crypto agent: goal in, stack and install steps out
